children: Planet Labs reported strong quarterly earnings Thursday after the market closed.

The Earth imaging company with hundreds of satellites in orbit reported second-quarter earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization, or Ebitda, of $13.9 million from sales of $116.1 million.

Wall Street was looking for Ebitda of $2.3 million from sales of $104.5 million. A year ago, sales were $73.4 million. Second-quarter sales topped the high end of Planet Labs' own guidance range of $107 million.

Space is growing in importance for commercial enterprises and militaries around the world. Defense and intelligence business accounted for 70% of revenue in the quarter, up from 57% a year ago. Those percentages mean defense revenue almost doubled to $81 million in the quarter.

The numbers look solid, although the guidance might give investors pause. The company expects third-quarter revenue of between $101 million and $105 million. Wall Street currently projects $114 million. Planet management also expects a third-quarter Ebitda loss of about $3.5 million. Wall Street projects positive Ebitda of $2.5 million.
Backlog ended the quarter at $815 million, up 11% year over year.
So far, the good outweighed any concerns. Shares were up almost 3% in after-hours trading at $18.88. Investors should brace for some volatility on Friday, though.

Planet Labs stock has a history of huge post-earnings moves. The stock has moved an average of 34%, up or down, following the past four quarterly reports. The smallest move was a 25.5% gain after fourth-quarter numbers were reported. At least they tend to go up. Shares have risen three times and fallen once over that span, although the most recent quarter was a 26% drop (after sales beat expectations).

Gains add up. Coming into Friday trading, shares were up more than 180% over the past 12 months. That's a huge gain, and there seemed to be some profit-taking ahead of earnings. Shares dropped more than 8% on Thursday, to $18.36, while the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average both gained more than 1%.
Space is the new high ground, and Planet Labs' technologies enable the U.S. military and its allies to take it.
